subject: Gaussian process and spatial predictive process: NA/NaN function evaluation

messages.author: 9721e69203f06751
messages.subject: Gaussian process and spatial predictive process: NA/NaN function evaluation
parts:
Hello,

I'm writing a spatial predictive process model, which is essentially a lower-dimensional version of a gaussian process model (see Latimer et al 2009, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1461-0248.2008.01270.x).

I've attached R and TMB code for both types of models. The gaussian process model (Mod1) works fine, but I'm getting NaN values for some SEs in the predictive process model (Mod2) because the Hessian isn't positive-definite. The model isn't over-parameterized and none of the predictors are enormously correlated, so I'm not sure what's causing the problem. I didn't encounter these issues when I coded the same models in Stan, so I'm wondering what steps I should take next to fix the problem.

Thanks,
SR

messages.author: 4453e5ef4c1cb06e
messages.subject: Re: Gaussian process and spatial predictive process: NA/NaN function evaluation
parts: If it works in Stan then try running tmbstan on Mod2 and see if you get the same posteriors as from Stan. If so, then I'd guess there's a numerical issue with the Laplace approximation. If not, that points to a model implementation issue.
